title: Control-plane race during VPC peering swap caused cross-tenant DNS responses
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple Dedicated customers reported intermittent DNS responses that appeared to be routed through incorrect tenant SNAT bindings shortly after scheduled VPC peering reconfigurations. Impact: potential cross-tenant visibility of DNS responses (transient), manifesting as wrong-RR or delayed replies and occasional connection failures for customer control planes. Root cause hypothesis (confirmed): a race between the peering/route reconciliation control-plane update and the dataplane connection-tracking (conntrack) lifecycle. When peer routes were changed during peering swap, the dataplane briefly accepted return packets that matched stale conntrack entries tied to the previous peering state. Those conntrack entries lacked a robust tenant guard, so SNAT/DNAT applied using stale mappings and forwarded replies across tenant boundaries until conntrack aged out or was flushed.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create two tenants A and B on Dedicated cluster with active VPC peering. 2) Start a long-lived UDP/TCP flow from a customer endpoint in tenant A to a service reachable via peered route. 3) Trigger a peering swap (remove and re-add peering or perform a route migration) causing rapid dataplane route changes. 4) Observe return-path packets hitting stale conntrack tuples and being translated with the old SNAT mapping. 5) Reproduce observed wrong-DNS reply or misrouted response behavior within 30s of swap.
root_cause_analysis: During peering reconfiguration we observed a window where route tables on the forwarding nodes changed before conntrack garbage-collection acknowledged the in-flight tuples. Conntrack tuples do not currently carry a tenant-guard tag that is consulted at translation time; translations were chosen solely by 5-tuple + SNAT state. When a packet arrived that matched an existing tuple but the active route had moved, the dataplane applied the existing NAT binding and forwarded the packet along the stale path. This produced transient cross-tenant routing of DNS replies in a worst-case timing alignment with long-lived flows.
remediation_plan: Short-term hotfix: add immediate conntrack flush hook in the peering reconciliation path to clear conntrack tuples for affected interfaces and VNIs during peering swap; backfill metric and alert for conntrack-flush failures. Medium-term fix: tag conntrack entries with tenant-id in conntrack mark and validate tenant-id on translation (drop if mismatch). Longer-term: implement per-tenant conntrack namespaces and add end-to-end integration tests that simulate peering swaps under traffic. See PRs and tests linked below.
implementation_details: - Hotfix PR (runtime): github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12456 - Adds conntrack flush step via nftables conntrack helper during peering reconciliation. - Core change PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12489 - Adds tenant-id stamp on conntrack mark and per-packet tenant validation before applying NAT. - Integration tests: github.com/redwood-inference/tests/pull/487 - Synthetic peering-swap tests with long-lived flows and assertion on no cross-tenant packets.
deploy_plan: 1) Merge hotfix and deploy to canary Dedicated cluster (canary-dedicated-3) for 2 hours while monitoring peering/dns error metrics. 2) If no regression, promote hotfix to all Dedicated clusters during low-traffic window. 3) Roll out core tenant-marking change to canary behind feature flag; enable after 24h stable. 4) Schedule coordinated rollout with on-call and SRE; provide rollback plan to revert feature flag and flush conntrack across cluster if issues observed.
acceptance_criteria: No cross-tenant DNS responses observed in canary during peering-swap test suite (0 occurrences over 1h)
Conntrack flush hook successfully executes in peering reconciliation path without errors (logs/metric)
Tenant-marking change prevents translation for mismatched tenant-id (unit+integration tests)
postmortem_tasks: Finalize postmortem doc and share with customers in INC-2026-147 thread
Add automated test job to simulate peering swaps in CI for Dedicated clusters
Add alert: sudden spike in dns_misroute_count > 5/min
